{
  "claim": "https://w3id.org/delphi/resource/claim/turing-ddi",
  "source": "local",
  "nanopubs": [
    "math-bio-theorems/nanopubs/unsigned/turing-ddi.trig"
  ],
  "fields": {
    "rdfs:seeAlso": "https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.64.2953",
    "dct:source": "Alan Turing (1952) The chemical basis of morphogenesis",
    "delphi:hypothesisType": "model-theorem",
    "delphi:proposedTest": "Measure the reaction Jacobian and the diffusivities of a candidate morphogen pair independently, check that the inequality holds, and then confirm that perturbing the diffusivity ratio switches patterning on or off.",
    "delphi:context": "Assumptions: two species, smooth kinetics, linearization about a homogeneous steady state, fixed domain without growth or mechanics. Formal status: the linear instability conditions are proved; existence and stability of nonlinear patterns are proved for many specific models but not in general.",
    "skos:notation": "u_t = f(u,v) + D_u \\nabla^2 u, v_t = g(u,v) + D_v \\nabla^2 v; with tr J < 0 and det J > 0, instability at some wavenumber k iff D_v f_u + D_u g_v > 2\\sqrt{D_u D_v \\det J}, which requires D_u \\ne D_v",
    "rdf:type": [
      "https://w3id.org/delphi/ontology/TestableHypothesis",
      "https://w3id.org/delphi/ontology/Claim"
    ],
    "dct:description": "A homogeneous steady state of two reacting chemicals that is stable without diffusion can become unstable to spatial perturbations when the chemicals diffuse at different rates, spontaneously producing a pattern.",
    "rdfs:label": "Turing diffusion-driven instability"
  },
  "assessments": []
}
